description: S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST MSG TYPE 2 is answered, to the asking client only, with our published node information: this node's address and transmit speed, and per peer its soft link state and what the last burst heard from it showed; other MSG TYPEs are ignored.
note: Our published encoding, docs/management-messages.md MSG TYPE 2 (interp S-0164; S-0035, S-0038, S-0114). The channel is held busy from 0 (P5-4), so nothing goes on air. Conn 2 never binds: its S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST MSG TYPE 2 with an empty body is valid without a binding (S-0032, S-0162) and is answered at once to conn 2 only with S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION MSG TYPE 2 (S-0034, S-0037). Body: this node's address as a 4-byte S_primitive address field (SIZE 7, individual: e0 00 01 02, Fig S-19, S-0058), the transmit waveform number 2 and interleaver code 4 (long) from drc.default_speed, and the peer count, 0. Its MSG TYPE 99 request is ignored with no reply (interp S-0038). Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for ARQ and sends 'hi' to 0.0.1.6, which is held for a soft link while the CAS calls (A-0008, A-0193): link_state calling. Two bursts are heard, each one type 7 D_PDU addressed to 0.0.1.4, not to us, so nothing is acted on (C-0566, C-0868) but the sender's receive quality is recorded at the burst end (C-0833): from 0.0.1.3, burst ended at 6000, wn 2 long, SNR 12.3 dB; from 0.0.1.5, ended at 9000, wn 3 short, SNR -5.7 dB. At 10500 conn 2 asks again. The answer lists three peers in address order, each a 13-byte record: address field; soft link state (0 none, 1 being made or held off); transmit wn and interleaver to the peer (the default speed); the wn and interleaver of the last burst heard (ff ff when never heard); its SNR in tenths of a dB, signed 16-bit big-endian (007b = 123, ffc7 = -57, 8000 when never heard); and whole seconds since that burst end (4 and 1; ffff when never heard). Interleaver codes: 0 ultra short to 5 very long.
